title: fix(cron): keep false-trigger automations quiet
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled automation whose condition returns false can append an unexpected “did not start” message to its owner conversation and change conversation recency. The finished event dropped `triggerFired: false`, so the Gateway could not distinguish a quiet condition from an actionable skipped run.

## User Impact

False conditions remain quiet, as the documented condition contract requires. Other skipped-run and pre-start error notices, completion webhooks, and execution authorization keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing boolean through the terminal event and stop explicitly quiet skipped events before session database access. This adds no state, schema, SQL, or public event field. Pre-acceptance and execution-effect authority checks remain unchanged.

The first PR CI run also exposed two stale exact fallback-payload expectations from #188105. Failure alerts already carry the job ID so repair turns can identify the failed job; retain the exact assertion and include that ID. The nearby fixture uses the shared required-value assertion and removes a one-use forwarding helper, preserving its history and state checks.

The durable-acceptance fixture repair originally in this branch landed independently in #188704. This branch integrates that owner unchanged, alongside #188624 and the Knip repair #188691.

## Evidence

- Scheduled baseline: run 41115244650, real-Gateway job 124268241491, quiet-automation recency assertion at line 462. The affected producer and notice path were unchanged through the original base.
- Explicit-false regression fails on the unchanged producer (`undefined` instead of `false`); focused cron suites pass 29/29. Notification-owner suite passes 23/23, including the early-return placement.
- Both stale delivery assertions reproduced locally; the complete delivery-outcomes fixture passes 6/6 after the correction. The supported source-fixture mode `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1` is not compiled Gateway proof.
- Two isolated Codex reviews and the production placement review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The final integrated review and exact-head CI are recorded below.
- Local compiled-Gateway proof stopped at declaration containment of the campaign-required external virtual store. No live-flow pass is inferred from that setup failure. All four final files pass formatting and type-aware lint; published CI supplies the remaining static gates.
- Final delta against integrated main: production +4 lines; tests −2; total +2. No latency or SQL saving claimed. No permission, schema, retention, or transcript identity changes.

Final integration head: `ebd503bcccd7b9de09d402227e24fd3c3c330d6c`, based on main `fc3490aa24e624f0182ae5e29482611fee5736fb`. The final delivery-outcomes run exits successfully with all 6 tests passing. The final isolated Codex review is scoped-clean at P0–P2; it assessed the supplied four-file diff without executing tests or inspecting unchanged source. The earlier production-owner reviews and test results remain applicable to the unchanged production fix.

CI run 41133139187 on the preceding integration head found a variable-shadowing lint error in the delivery fixture. The final two-line correction renames the stored-job binding; formatting and type-aware lint pass for all four files. One additional isolated correction-only Codex review is scoped-clean at P0–P2. The final head passed CI run 41136290633, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards and all static and behavioral checks. The aggregate gate is recorded at landing.

Open-PR check on final head: paired main-only versus main-plus-candidate comparisons add no conflicts for #188306 (`704a92c588da`), #187269 (`8a1b8a0df773`), #187268 (`f03a5086ef0a`), or #186366 (`a6a54c9b7d7a`). Duplicate #188715 (`bcc559a04c63`) produced one conflict in the failure-alert expectation, then was closed by the coordinator as duplicate; it no longer targets main. The exact payload assertion remains intact.
